subject.title: fix(agent): recover disconnected gateway runs before rerunning

question: After an accepted Gateway disconnect, should `openclaw agent` recover-first and then automatically start the existing isolated embedded fallback when recovery is exhausted, or should it fail closed unless the user explicitly opts into rerunning?
rationale: Either policy is technically plausible, but it determines user-visible latency, whether an already accepted turn can be executed twice, and what CLI output users receive after an ambiguous disconnect; repository policy treats such fallback changes as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Approve recovery-first with isolated fallback
options.body: Wait and cache-replay the original Gateway run first, then retain the isolated `gateway-fallback-*` run only after recovery cannot establish a terminal outcome.

options.title: Require fail-closed ambiguity handling
options.body: Stop after an unresolved recovery outcome and expose a rerun only through an explicit, documented user opt-in.

options.title: Retain current fallback-first behavior
options.body: Keep the current immediate isolated fallback contract and pause or substantially narrow this recovery-first branch.

recommendation.title: Approve recovery-first with isolated fallback
recommendation.body: Wait and cache-replay the original Gateway run first, then retain the isolated `gateway-fallback-*` run only after recovery cannot establish a terminal outcome.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged fresh-session fallback behavior that forms the current compatibility contract.
